$comment: Derma Intel v4 — the DARK-SURFACE probe map. v3 measured a light UI on a hue-neutral field and never needed a dark rung; v4's cards float over a background subject, so the glass ladder grows a dark side. Coordinates are FRACTIONS of image width/height so the map survives any resize. Read with docs/redesign/v4/tools/sample_reference.py, which adds a maxluma mode (light glyphs on a dark ground) and enforces the dark/light luma gates that v3 declared but never checked. Probe coordinates were AIMED, not guessed: a scratch locator scanned each image on a 60x40 grid for flat dark plateaus (p95-p05 < 14) and for light-text-on-dark cells (p50 < 105 and p95 > 175), and the coordinates below are those cells' centres.
$method: The v3 reconciliation rule still governs: RELATIVE relationships come from raw deltas within one image; ABSOLUTE values come from cross-image consensus. For the dark rung the load-bearing measurement is the STEP — a card probe paired with a subject probe just outside that same card, in the same image, so the photographic cast cancels. Paired probes share a name stem: <thing>-subject / <thing>-card.
$honesty: These references are 3D device renders of a photographed body under warm studio light. Every dark sample therefore carries a warm cast (R > G > B). Our identity is hue-neutral by measurement (ATLAS.md section 1: every v3 neutral probe returned R=G=B exactly), so the cast is an artefact of the reference and is NEUTRALISED downstream — we take the STEP and the ALPHA, never the hue. See ATLAS-DARK.md.

images.$why: The purest structural reference for a dark rung: translucent panels over a warm dark ground with a hairline border, which is exactly the primitive v4 needs. Raw only - there is no white surface in this image to anchor a gain, and it is a JPEG, so compression noise inflates sigma. Taken for the STEP and the border, never for hue.
